QuestionStmt.S: The equation of the plane containing the line $\frac{x-2}{3} = \frac{y+1}{2} = \frac{z-4}{-2}$ and the point $(0, 5, 0)$ is

Solution.S:
Let the equation of the plane passing through $(0, 5, 0)$ be:

$$a(x - 0) + b(y - 5) + c(z - 0) = 0$$
$$\Rightarrow ax + b(y - 5) + cz = 0$$

The line passes through $(2, -1, 4)$, so this point lies on the plane:

$$a(2) + b(-1 - 5) + c(4) = 0 \Rightarrow 2a - 6b + 4c = 0$$
$$\Rightarrow a - 3b + 2c = 0 \quad \text{(i)}$$

The direction ratios of the line are $(3, 2, -2)$. Since the plane contains the line, the normal to the plane is perpendicular to the direction vector of the line:

$$3a + 2b - 2c = 0 \quad \text{(ii)}$$

Solving (i) and (ii):

From (i): $a = 3b - 2c$.

Substitute into (ii): $3(3b - 2c) + 2b - 2c = 0$
$$9b - 6c + 2b - 2c = 0 \Rightarrow 11b - 8c = 0 \Rightarrow b = \frac{8}{11}c$$

Then $a = 3\left(\frac{8}{11}c\right) - 2c = \frac{24}{11}c - \frac{22}{11}c = \frac{2}{11}c$.

Thus $a : b : c = \frac{2}{11} : \frac{8}{11} : 1 = 2 : 8 : 11$.

So $a = 2, b = 8, c = 11$.

Substitute into the plane equation:

$$2x + 8(y - 5) + 11z = 0$$
$$2x + 8y - 40 + 11z = 0$$
$$2x + 8y + 11z - 40 = 0$$

Final Answer: $$\boxed{2x + 8y + 11z - 40 = 0}$$

Hence, the correct option is B.
